hypotheses.interpretation: A team that owns the opponent-adjusted sustained-efficiency matchup moves the ball more reliably per snap than its opponent allows; over ~70 snaps that should convert into winning more often.
hypotheses.name: CONTROL (any tier) -> winner / moneyline

hypotheses.interpretation: A moderate efficiency edge is a smaller, less visible advantage; if the market anchors on records, rankings or raw scoring it could under-rate it. Required study (prompt section 11).
hypotheses.name: MODERATE CONTROL -> closing spread (ATS)

hypotheses.interpretation: A strong efficiency edge is the most visible kind; it should be well priced. Tests whether the market fully prices the separation.
hypotheses.name: STRONG CONTROL -> closing spread (ATS)

hypotheses.interpretation: A per-play efficiency edge compounds over more snaps: more possessions should mean more separation for the CONTROL side. Spreads may scale with talent gaps but not with expected snap count.
hypotheses.name: CONTROL x PACE (control-side margin and ATS vs possession environment)

hypotheses.interpretation: Trailing teams come back through the air. When the CONTROL team's pass defense outclasses the opponent's pass offense (opponent passing direction edge <= -1.0), the weaker side has few fast comeback paths, so the CONTROL side should convert its edge into wins more reliably.
hypotheses.name: CONTROL x DEFENSIVE SUPPRESSION (opponent passing offense outclassed) -> winner

hypotheses.interpretation: When neither offense owns the efficiency matchup (EVEN_MATCHUP resolves), the game should be closer than an average game; if the spread still reflects a talent/brand gap, the underdog should cover.
hypotheses.name: CLOSENESS -> market underdog ATS

hypotheses.interpretation: Fewer possessions shrink the variance of the margin; an even matchup with few snaps favours the points.
hypotheses.name: EVEN MATCHUP x LOW PACE -> market underdog ATS

hypotheses.interpretation: More snaps -> more scoring opportunities, beyond what the scoring baseline already counts.
hypotheses.name: PACE claim HIGH -> over

hypotheses.interpretation: Fewer snaps -> fewer possessions -> fewer points.
hypotheses.name: PACE claim LOW -> under

hypotheses.interpretation: As 008/009 on the continuous production pace measure.
hypotheses.name: Possession environment (continuous) -> total residual

hypotheses.interpretation: Both defenses out-rate the offenses they face; drives stall on both sides.
hypotheses.name: DEFENSIVE SUPPRESSION claim -> under

hypotheses.interpretation: Both offenses efficient / high-scoring environment beyond the baseline (V2: incremental on holdout).
hypotheses.name: SCORING ENVIRONMENT ELEVATED -> over

hypotheses.interpretation: Low-scoring environment (V2: NOT incremental over the baseline on holdout).
hypotheses.name: SCORING ENVIRONMENT SUPPRESSED -> under

hypotheses.interpretation: An aerial mismatch (pass offense vs pass defense) may separate games beyond generic efficiency.
hypotheses.name: Passing matchup net, beyond sustained efficiency -> margin / ATS

hypotheses.interpretation: A ground mismatch controls clock and down-and-distance beyond generic efficiency.
hypotheses.name: Rushing matchup net, beyond sustained efficiency -> margin / ATS

hypotheses.interpretation: A team that owns efficiency AND the run game can shorten the game while ahead and finish drives.
hypotheses.name: RUSH EDGE x CONTROL (same-side rushing net >= 1) -> ATS

hypotheses.interpretation: A repeatable sack/TFL edge matters most against an offense that already allows sacks (opponent offense sack-rate quality <= -0.5 SD): drive-killing negative plays.
hypotheses.name: DISRUPTION x WEAK PROTECTION -> disruption side ATS

hypotheses.interpretation: Explosive plays create points without sustained drives.
hypotheses.name: EXPLOSIVE advantage
hypotheses.reason: CFBD 2014-2025 caches carry no explosive-play counts (production explosive metrics are None on every historical row; net.explosiveness is null). Only the 2026 ESPN log has them (weeks 1-6). Not tested; not imputed from CFBD PPA 'explosiveness', which is a different quantity.

hypotheses.interpretation: A team that converts scoring opportunities better but does not own efficiency: finishing is noisier and partly luck, so the market may over-weight points-based reputations (expected sign NEGATIVE for the finishing side vs the spread is equally plausible; test is two-sided, reported direction +).
hypotheses.name: FINISHING edge without efficiency edge -> ATS

hypotheses.interpretation: The CONTROL quantity itself, continuous: does it carry margin information the closing spread lacks?
hypotheses.name: Sustained-efficiency net (continuous) -> margin / ATS

hypotheses.name: Scoring-baseline margin vs closing spread disagreement -> ATS

hypotheses.interpretation: gap.total = baseline total - closing total.
hypotheses.name: Scoring-baseline total vs closing total disagreement -> total residual
